root_cause.text: The error path in qfq_change_class() unconditionally frees the class and its qdisc even when modifying an existing class, causing a use-after-free because those resources are still referenced by the Qdisc.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a guard `if (!existing)` before `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc); kfree(cl);` to ensure only newly allocated classes are freed. The commit message explicitly states that freeing an existing class’s qdisc and cl leads to UAF.

Author: Vlad Buslov <vladbu@mellanox.com>
Date:   Mon Sep 24 19:22:50 2018 +0300

    net: sched: rename qdisc_destroy() to qdisc_put()
    
    Current implementation of qdisc_destroy() decrements Qdisc reference
    counter and only actually destroy Qdisc if reference counter value reached
    zero. Rename qdisc_destroy() to qdisc_put() in order for it to better
    describe the way in which this function currently implemented and used.
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows that in qfq_change_class() the error path (label 'destroy_class') unconditionally calls qdisc_put() (renamed from qdisc_destroy()) and kfree(cl). This matches the root cause: the class and its qdisc are freed even when modifying an existing class, leading to use-after-free. The commit only renames the function, no fix is applied. Thus the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.

bic_trace_step.reason: In qfq_change_class(), when modifying an existing class (existing=true), the code jumps to 'set_change_agg'. There, if allocation of new_agg fails (kzalloc returns NULL), it goes to 'destroy_class', which unconditionally calls qdisc_destroy(cl->qdisc) and kfree(cl). This frees the existing class that is still referenced by the Qdisc, causing a use-after-free. The error path does not check for the existing case or avoid freeing the class. See lines with 'set_change_agg:', 'if (new_agg == NULL) { ... goto destroy_class; }' and 'destroy_class: qdisc_destroy(cl->qdisc); kfree(cl);'.
